question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt `channels.msteams.accounts` and `channels.msteams.defaultAccount` as the public multi-bot contract, with legacy root config as the implicit default account, explicit named-account identity/port requirements, and account-scoped auth/session state?
rationale: This is a durable public channel configuration and upgrade contract; source review, CI, and live proof can validate behavior but cannot choose the permanent Teams API and operator compatibility policy.

options.title: Accept the current contract
options.body: Treat the account map, default-account compatibility, per-account listener model, and scoped state/auth behavior as the supported Teams multi-account API after exact-head checks remain green.

options.title: Request contract revisions
options.body: Ask for targeted schema, listener, migration, or credential-resolution changes before merging if this is not the desired Teams API.

options.title: Pause for broader design
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and pause this PR if Teams multi-account support should wait for a cross-channel account or shared-listener design.

recommendation.title: Accept the current contract
recommendation.body: Treat the account map, default-account compatibility, per-account listener model, and scoped state/auth behavior as the supported Teams multi-account API after exact-head checks remain green.

likelyOwner.reason: BradGroux is the clearest Microsoft/Teams contract reviewer from the duplicate closure, tracker ownership, and contributor request for guidance.
